problem: Existing embodied instruction following (EIF) methods assume a known environment where all interactable object categories are given, so in unknown house-level scenes they generate infeasible plans that manipulate non-existent objects. They are also designed for single-room scenes.
motivation: Household robots work in homes where object locations and existence change constantly, so pre-built maps are unreliable. The agent must build scene maps online and explore efficiently, generating feasible plans only with objects that actually exist.
key_idea: A hierarchical MLLM (LLaVA) agent, with a high-level planner and a low-level frontier/interaction controller, is grounded by an online CLIP-feature top-down semantic map with instruction-conditioned dynamic region attention, so planning and exploration are aligned.
insight: Active exploration is the main driver: removing exploration drops large-scale SR from 45.09 to 11.27, and non-frontier exploration is also worse (36.76). Rich implicit features matter (category-only map 36.36 vs 45.77 SR), while dynamic attention gives a smaller gain (44.78 without it). Fine-tuned 7B LLaVA on synthetic data far outperforms prompted GPT-4o (30.54 SR), and replacing the planner with BERT templates drops SR to 24.38.
method: Hierarchical agent: a high-level planner P^h predicts the next natural-language step from the instruction, completed steps and the semantic map; a low-level controller P^l outputs action primitive, location and target object.
Online semantic feature map: pixelwise features (whole-image plus instance-mask features) are projected to a top-down map using depth and updated incrementally during exploration.

Frontier representation: frontiers between known and unknown regions are extracted from the occupancy map via connected components (regions under 150 px removed); 32 visual tokens are sampled per frontier, with centroid coordinates as text, up to 256 tokens.

Dynamic region attention: a CLIP score of the image against the task-object prompts (L_dec, with L_dec-bar and L_none as contrast prompts) gives the weight w_i = c_i / mean(c_k), used in the map update S_i=(1-w_i)S_{i-1}+w_i F_i.

Data generation: GPT-4 expands seed instructions into plans for 2509 ProcTHOR scenes; PDDL filters logical errors; the plans are executed with A* to collect trajectories and RGB-D for planner and controller samples.

Training: LoRA SFT of LLaVA-7B (Vicuna-1.3-7B) with a CE loss on the planner and controller outputs, plus counterfactual samples in which target objects are removed or replaced by similar-usage objects.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-7B (Vicuna-1.3-7B) planner and controller, LoRA fine-tuned; CLIP features for the map
setting.training_data: Synthetic GPT-4-generated data in ProcTHOR: about 2k instructions (1386 target-specific short, 333 long, 332 abstract) across 2509 scenes, giving 30k ground-truth plans plus A* expert trajectories
setting.observation: Egocentric 600x600 RGB-D, with an online top-down semantic feature map
setting.action_space: Primitives Navigate/PickUp/Place/Open/Close/ToggleOn/ToggleOff/Slice with location and target; navigation to frontier coordinates, moves of 0.25 m and 90° rotations
setting.privileged: none (ground-truth plans/actions used only in an ablation)

numbers_note: ProcTHOR EIF is the paper's own benchmark (201/67/152 test instructions per subset), so it uses the 'other:' benchmark name and the split 'test' is an assumption. Ablation-only variants are omitted.
results: On ProcTHOR target-specific short tasks the method reaches 45.77 SR in normal-scale and 45.09 in large-scale scenes, versus LLM-Planner at 28.36 / 18.63 and FILM at 5.97 / 0.49. It also leads on long and abstract tasks, though absolute SR stays low (13.43 / 10.53 in normal-scale scenes).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation, with no real-robot manipulation.
Navigation policy ignores compatibility with manipulation (e.g. stopping too close to targets, failing to see closed spaces); most failures are navigation failures.
Low success on long-horizon and abstract instructions (about 10-20% SR).
